topic: Do opposites attract? Similarity and attraction
title: Do Opposites Attract? What 313 Studies Found
voiceover: Do opposites really attract? In 2008, Montoya, Horton and Kirchner combined 313 studies on similarity and attraction. They compared actual similarity, meaning real shared traits, with perceived similarity, meaning what people believe they share. Perceived similarity predicted attraction more strongly than actual similarity did. The effect of actual similarity was large overall. But it depended on whether the people had actually interacted. So in this analysis, believing you're alike may matter at least as much as actually being alike. This research measured similarity and attraction, not every kind of difference. Meta-analyses summarize many studies, and their conclusions depend on which studies were included. So in this research, feeling similar went with liking more than actually being similar did. Tomorrow: does using someone's name make them more likely to say yes?

New psychology short every day on The Psyche Discourse. Source: Montoya, R. M., Horton, R. S., & Kirchner, J. (2008). Is actual similarity necessary for attraction? accuracy_note: The video reports the meta-analysis conclusions about similarity (perceived vs actual) and does not claim to settle every kind of difference. The details of the interaction moderator are stated loosely, as in the abstract.
